steps: On the CNC Turning Center, a finish turning operation is performed on a lathed part for 17 minutes, using CNC program #7A for final contouring, with tool offsets verified and set for all eight tools and a spindle speed of 1200 rpm for the finishing pass, resulting in a finished machined component that is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

The planed part is subjected to surface grinding on a grinding machine for 25 minutes using an aluminum oxide grinding wheel with 60 grit at a wheel speed of 3500 sfm and a feed rate of 0.005 ipr, resulting in a ground part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Horizontal Lathe, a metal bar is subjected to rough turning for 65 minutes, using a carbide insert tool (CNMG 432) at a spindle speed of 800 rpm and a feed rate of 0.012 ipr, resulting in a lathed part that is then transferred to a conveyor belt.

On a Broaching Machine, an internal broaching operation is performed on a lathed part using a 16-tooth spline broach to achieve a precision level of ±0.0005 in tolerance, taking 31 minutes to complete, after which the resulting broached component is transferred to a MobileRobot.

On the Gear Shaper, gear shaping is performed on the broached component to produce a shaped gear, operating at a shaping speed of 180 strokes per minute to form a 24-tooth spur gear, taking 80 minutes, after which the shaped gear is placed on the ConveyorBelt.

On the Honing Machine, a cylinder honing operation is performed on a honed cylinder taken from the ConveyorBelt, using a 220 mesh honing grit to achieve a bore size of 1.5005 ± 0.0001 in, lasting for 64 minutes, resulting in a precision finished part that is transferred to the MobileRobot as a ground part.

The Bandsaw performs Cut-Off Sawing on a metal bar loaded from the MobileRobot, cutting it to size using a bi-metal blade with 4/6 TPI at a saw speed of 120 fpm and a cutting width of 0.035 in kerf, taking 30 minutes to complete, and outputs the resulting lathed part onto the ConveyorBelt.

On the Stewart Platform Mills, the Precision Milling operation machines the Milled part into a Ground part using 5-axis simultaneous tool configuration with a D12 end mill, maintaining a milling precision of ±0.0002 in and employing an active damping system to minimize vibrations, and the process runs for 36 minutes before the resulting Ground part is transferred to a MobileRobot.

A 3-axis milling operation is performed on a vertical milling machine using an HSS end mill with a 1/2 inch diameter at a spindle speed of 1500 rpm and a depth of cut of 0.100 in per pass, processing the lathed part for 99 minutes to produce a milled part, which is then placed on a conveyor belt.

On a Horizontal Milling Machine, perform finish milling on the milled part for 16 minutes at a milling speed of 2000 rpm using a climb milling tool path with full contour engagement to achieve a surface finish of 32 microinches, resulting in a finished machined component that is transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Hobbing Machine, a broached component is subjected to gear hobbing to produce a hobbied gear with an involute profile and 14.5° pressure angle, operating at a hobbing speed of 110 rpm and a feed rate of 0.015 ipr, and the operation runs for 32 minutes, after which the hobbied gear is transferred to a conveyor belt.

Using a Drill Press, precision drilling is performed on the broached component for 3 minutes to create holes with a diameter of 0.250 in and a tolerance of ±0.0003 in, resulting in a finished part with holes that is then transferred to a MobileRobot.

Using a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine), a fine wire cutting operation is performed on a ground part for 28 minutes in high-precision skim cut finishing mode, utilizing double-pass deburr settings and deionized water with a resistivity of 1 MΩ-cm as the dielectric fluid, resulting in a precision finished milled part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

A milled part is loaded from a conveyor belt onto a shaper to perform keyway shaping using an HSS single-point cutter at a shaping speed of 30 strokes per minute and a stroke length of 6.0 in, producing a shaped part that is transferred to a mobile robot, and the operation runs for 79 minutes.

The Planer performs surface planing on the Milled part for 1 minute, removing material to a depth of 0.005 in with a feed rate of 0.020 ipr to achieve a surface finish of 63 microinches, resulting in a Planed part that is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

On a Vertical Lathe, a drilled component is subjected to facing and turning operations involving multi-pass facing and OD turning with a precision level of ±0.0004 in, resulting in a final drilled and shaped part, and the process runs for 50 minutes before the output is transferred to a MobileRobot.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on sheet metal for 94 minutes, using a 3000 W laser with a cutting speed of 45 ipm and nitrogen gas assist at 200 psi, resulting in cut sheet metal that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) performs straight-line shearing on sheet metal for 31 minutes, using a tool steel hardened blade with a shear angle of 1.5° and a cutting speed of 10 strokes per minute, transforming the input sheet metal on the conveyor belt into sheared sheet metal that is transferred to a mobile robot.

The punch press performs turret punching on a sheet metal component loaded by a mobile robot, using a 0.5 in round punch at a stroke speed of 200 spm with automatically calibrated die alignment, producing a finished sheet metal product that is transferred to a conveyor belt after processing for 87 minutes.

On a Screw Machines, an Automatic Screw Threading operation is performed on a Lathed part fed from a ConveyorBelt, creating a Screwed component with #10-32 UNC threads at a production rate of 120 parts per hour, and the process runs for 94 minutes before the resulting MilledPart is transferred to a MobileRobot.

The milled part is shaped using a shaper machine with a high-speed steel (HSS) single-point tool, a stroke length of 250 mm, and a shaping speed of 30 strokes per minute, transforming it into a shaped part that is then placed on a conveyor belt, all taking 71 minutes.

On a Hobbing Machine, a gear hobbing operation is performed on a broached component to produce an involute spur gear with a 20° pressure angle, running at a hobbing speed of 120 rpm and a feed rate of 0.5 mm/rev, taking 86 minutes to complete, after which the hobbied gear is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

A precision wire cutting operation is performed on a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) using a 0.25 mm brass wire with deionized water dielectric and electrical parameters of 120 V, 10 A, and RC pulse mode at a cutting speed of 8 mm/min, processing the shaped part for 16 minutes to produce a precision finished part, which is then transferred to a conveyor belt.

On a Bandsaw, a metal bar is cut using a bi-metal variable pitch blade with 4 TPI at a saw speed of 60 m/min and a cutting width of 3 mm kerf in a bar cutting operation lasting 79 minutes, resulting in a lathed part conveyed to a conveyor belt.

On the Gear Shaper, an internal gear shaping operation is performed on a broached component to produce a shaped gear with an internal spur gear profile featuring 36 teeth, using a shaping speed of 150 strokes per minute, and the process runs for 92 minutes, after which the shaped gear is placed on a conveyor belt.

A metal bar is loaded onto a mobile robot and then undergoes rough turning on a horizontal lathe using a carbide insert tool (CNMG 432) at a rotation speed of 450 rpm and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a conveyor belt, all taking 79 minutes.

Using a grinding machine, a surface grinding operation is performed on a planed part loaded on a mobile robot, utilizing an aluminum oxide grinding wheel with 60 grit at a wheel speed of 1800 rpm and a feed rate of 2 m/min, transforming it into a ground part that is then transferred to a conveyor belt, all for 63 minutes.

On the CNC Turning Center, a finish turning operation is performed on a lathed part for 10 minutes using CNC program #102 - Finish contour and chamfer, with spindle speed set to 800 rpm and tool offsets of X: 0.02 mm and Z: 0.01 mm, resulting in a finished machined component that is transferred to the conveyor belt.

On a Vertical Lathe, a metal bar is loaded from a MobileRobot and undergoes facing and turning operations for 47 minutes, using a cermet insert tool (DNMG 300) at a spindle speed of 500 rpm and a feed rate of 0.25 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

The milled part is subjected to surface planing on a planer for 64 minutes, achieving a planing depth of 2 mm, a feed rate of 1.5 m/min, and a surface finish of Ra 3.2 µm, resulting in a planed part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

A lathed part is face milled using a vertical milling machine equipped with a 50 mm diameter indexable face mill at a milling speed of 120 m/min and a depth of cut of 3 mm, transforming it into a milled part, which is then placed on a conveyor belt, with the operation lasting for 56 minutes.

The honing machine performs precision honing on a honed cylinder, using a 150 mesh honing grit to achieve a bore size of 25.00 ± 0.005 mm, for 4 minutes, resulting in a precision finished part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

On the Drill Press, a center drilling operation is performed on a metal bar loaded by a MobileRobot, using a 6.5 mm drill at a spindle speed of 900 rpm and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, lasting for 87 minutes, resulting in a drilled component that is placed on a ConveyorBelt.

On a Broaching Machine, an internal broaching operation is performed on a metal bar using a pull-type square broach with a feed rate of 1 pass at 5 m/min and a depth of cut of 4 mm total rise, taking 16 minutes to produce a broached component that is then placed on a conveyor belt.

Using a punch press, a sheet metal component is subjected to a sheet metal punching operation for 43 minutes, employing a 10 mm round punch at a stroke speed of 80 strokes per minute and hydraulic die alignment with ±0.05 mm tolerance, resulting in a finished cut sheet metal product that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on sheet metal for 70 minutes, using a laser power of 3000 W, a cutting speed of 2.5 m/min, and nitrogen gas assist at 12 bar, transforming the input material into cut sheet metal, which is then placed on a conveyor belt.

The Horizontal Milling Machine performs final slot milling on the milled part for 15 minutes, using a CNC-guided linear interpolation tool path and a milling speed of 150 m/min to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, resulting in a finished machined component that is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

On a Screw Machines, an Automatic Screw Threading operation is performed on a Lathed part loaded from a MobileRobot, creating metric coarse threads with 6g tolerance and M10 screw size at a production rate of 120 parts per hour, resulting in a Screwed component placed on a ConveyorBelt, and the process runs for 27 minutes.

A milled part is machined using multi-axis precision milling on a Stewart Platform Mills for 99 minutes, achieving a milling precision of ±0.005 mm with a 6-axis synchronized ball end mill tool configuration and an active piezoelectric damping system for vibration control, resulting in a ground part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) performs straight shearing on sheet metal loaded from a MobileRobot, using a tungsten carbide edge blade hardened to 65 HRC with a shear angle of 1.5° and a cutting speed of 10 m/min, processing for 37 minutes to produce sheared sheet metal that is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

On a CNC Turning Center, a finish turning operation is performed on a lathed part loaded from a MobileRobot, using CNC program Program_8872, tool offsets TO_03, and a spindle speed of 1250 rpm, resulting in a finished machined component placed on a ConveyorBelt after processing for 81 minutes.

On a Broaching Machine, internal broaching is performed on a lathed part using a pull-type spline broach with high precision, taking 32 minutes to complete, after which the resulting broached component is transferred to a MobileRobot.

Using a Punch Press, a sheet metal component is punched with a 12 mm round punch at a stroke speed of 80 strokes per minute and automatic die centering for 76 minutes, transforming it into a finished cut sheet metal product that is then transferred to a mobile robot.

Using a horizontal milling machine, a precision face milling operation is performed on the milled part for 80 minutes, employing a climb milling tool path with 75% stepover and a milling speed of 650 rpm to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, after which the finished machined component is transferred to the conveyor belt.

On the Gear Shaper machine, a broached component is shaped into a spur gear with 24 teeth through the gear shaping operation at a speed of 180 strokes per minute, taking 19 minutes to complete, after which the resulting shaped gear is transferred to a mobile robot.

The drill press performs precision drilling on the broached component loaded in the mobile robot, creating holes with a diameter of 8.5 mm and a tolerance of +/- 0.02 mm, and outputs the finished part with holes to the conveyor belt, taking 6 minutes.

On a Vertical Lathe, the drilled component is machined using a facing and turning operation for 37 minutes, following a multi-pass facing toolpath with chamfering at high precision level, resulting in a final drilled and shaped part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on a sheet metal component loaded on a conveyor belt, using a 4000 W laser with nitrogen gas assist at a cutting speed of 3.2 m/min for 59 minutes, resulting in a cut sheet metal component transferred to a mobile robot.

The milled part is subjected to surface planing on a planer for 8 minutes, achieving a planing depth of 1.2 mm and a feed rate of 0.25 mm/rev to produce a planed part with a surface finish of Ra 3.2 µm, which is then transferred to a conveyor belt.

On a Screw Machines, thread rolling is performed on a lathed part to create a metric coarse thread of size M10, with a production rate of 120 units per hour, taking 3 minutes, after which the screwed component is transferred to a MobileRobot.

The Shaper performs a Keyway Shaping operation on the Milled part loaded from the MobileRobot, using an HSS single-point cutter with a stroke length of 75 mm and a shaping speed of 45 strokes per minute, producing a Shaped part that is transferred to the ConveyorBelt, and this operation takes 41 minutes.

The Stewart Platform Mills performs ultra-precision milling on the milled part, achieving a milling precision of ±0.005 mm using a 6-axis adaptive toolpath and an active damping system to minimize vibrations, processing the part for 79 minutes before transferring the resulting ground part to the mobile robot.

On a Bandsaw, a metal bar is cut into a lathed part through a bar cutting operation lasting 8 minutes, using a bi-metal variable pitch blade with a saw speed of 60 m/min and a cutting width of 3.2 mm, after which the lathed part is transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Hobbing Machine, a gear hobbing operation is performed on a broached component to create an involute gear profile with a 20° pressure angle, running at a hobbing speed of 210 rpm and a feed rate of 0.8 mm/rev, lasting for 83 minutes, resulting in a hobbied gear that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

The planed part is subjected to surface grinding on a grinding machine using an aluminum oxide grinding wheel with 60 grit at a wheel speed of 1800 rpm and a feed rate of 0.05 mm/pass, resulting in a ground part, and the operation runs for 68 minutes before the output is transferred to a mobile robot.

On the Honing Machine, the Cylinder Honing operation finishes the bore of the honed cylinder to a size of 45.0 mm +0.015/0 using a 220 mesh honing grit, taking 53 minutes to complete, after which the precision finished part is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

Using a shear (sheet metal) machine, a guillotine shearing operation is performed on sheet metal for 29 minutes, cutting the material with a hardened steel, double-edged blade at a cutting speed of 20 cuts per hour and a shear angle of 1.5°, resulting in sheared sheet metal that is transferred to a mobile robot.

A metal bar is loaded onto a mobile robot and then undergoes rough turning on a horizontal lathe using a carbide insert TNMG 16 04 08 tool at a rotation speed of 450 rpm and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a conveyor belt, all taking 61 minutes.

The Fine Wire EDM Cutting operation is performed on a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) for 24 minutes, using high-precision skim cut finishing mode, double spark-off with reverse polarity deburring settings, and deionized water as the dielectric fluid, to process a ground part from the ConveyorBelt into a precision finished part, which is then transferred to a MobileRobot.

A 3-axis milling operation is performed on a vertical milling machine using an end mill with a 12 mm diameter at a milling speed of 1100 rpm and a depth of cut of 2.5 mm, processing the lathed part for 53 minutes to produce a milled part, which is then placed on a conveyor belt.

On a Screw Machines, threading is performed on a lathed part to create metric coarse threads of size M12 at a production rate of 120 parts per hour, taking 78 minutes to complete, after which the resulting drilled component is placed on a conveyor belt.

The milled part is planed on a planer for 99 minutes, achieving a planing depth of 2.5 mm, a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev, and a surface finish of Ra 3.2 µm, resulting in a planed part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Horizontal Lathe, a metal bar is subjected to rough turning for 97 minutes using a carbide insert tool at a rotation speed of 450 rpm and a feed rate of 0.25 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Broaching Machine, an internal broaching operation is performed on a lathed part using a pull-type broach with a precision level of Class 7, taking 20 minutes to complete, after which the resulting broached component is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

The bandsaw cuts the metal bar to length in a cutting operation that lasts for 3 minutes, using a bi-metal blade with a saw speed of 80 m/min and a cutting width of 3 mm, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Shaper machine, a keyway is shaped into a Milled part using an HSS single-point tool at a shaping speed of 20 strokes per minute and a stroke length of 50 mm, taking 1 minutes to complete, after which the resulting Shaped part is transferred to a MobileRobot.

On the Gear Shaper, gear shaping is performed on the broached component to produce a shaped gear, forming a spur gear with 24 teeth at a shaping speed of 60 rpm, taking 97 minutes, after which the shaped gear is placed on a mobile robot.

The milled part is finish milled on a horizontal milling machine using climb milling with contour offset tool path at a milling speed of 220 m/min to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, resulting in a finished machined component, and this operation takes 92 minutes.

On a Hobbing Machine, a gear hobbing operation is performed on a broached component loaded from a conveyor belt, using a hobbing speed of 180 rpm and a feed rate of 0.5 mm/rev to cut an involute profile with a 20° pressure angle, resulting in a hobbied gear that is placed onto a mobile robot, and the process runs for 43 minutes.

A lathed part is face milled on a vertical milling machine using a carbide end mill at a milling speed of 250 m/min and a depth of cut of 3 mm, taking 11 minutes to complete, after which the resulting milled part is placed on a conveyor belt.

Using a Drill Press, a precision drilling operation is performed on a broached component to create holes with a diameter of 10 mm and a tolerance of +/- 0.05 mm, taking 25 minutes, after which the finished part with holes is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

On the CNC Turning Center, a finish turning operation is performed on the lathed part for 31 minutes using CNC program Program_023 with tool offsets verified and loaded and a spindle speed of 600 rpm, resulting in a finished machined component that is transferred to the conveyor belt.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) machine performs a shearing operation on sheet metal fed from a conveyor belt, cutting it into sheared sheet metal using a high-carbon steel blade at a shear angle of 2° and a cutting speed of 15 strokes per minute, with the processed parts transferred to a mobile robot, all taking 98 minutes.

The planed part is subjected to surface grinding on a grinding machine using an aluminum oxide grinding wheel with 60 grit at a wheel speed of 1800 rpm and a feed rate of 0.05 mm/pass, resulting in a ground part, and the operation lasts for 73 minutes, after which the ground part is transferred to a mobile robot.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on a sheet metal component loaded on a conveyor belt, using a 2500 W laser with nitrogen gas assist at a cutting speed of 2.5 m/min for 38 minutes, resulting in a cut sheet metal component transferred to a mobile robot.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs precision wire cutting on a ground part using deionized water as the dielectric fluid, with fine finish mode and deburring enabled, producing a precision finished part that is transferred to the conveyor belt, all for 71 minutes.

On the Stewart Platform Mills, a multi-axis precision milling operation is performed on the milled part from the ConveyorBelt for 69 minutes, achieving a milling precision of ±0.01 mm using 5-axis simultaneous control and an active damping system, resulting in a ground part transferred to the MobileRobot.

On the Vertical Lathe, the drilled component is machined using facing and turning operations involving CNC-controlled facing and diameter reduction with IT7 tolerance class precision, resulting in the final drilled and shaped part, which is then transferred to the conveyor belt, all taking 71 minutes.

The honing machine performs precision honing on a honed cylinder, using a 220 mesh honing grit to achieve a bore size of 50.00 mm ± 0.005 mm, resulting in a precision finished part, and the process runs for 73 minutes before the output is transferred to a mobile robot.

The punch press performs a punching operation on a sheet metal component, using a 12 mm round punch at a stroke speed of 100 strokes per minute with automatic die alignment, processing the material for 2 minutes to produce a finished sheet metal product that is then transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Bandsaw, a metal bar is cut through sawing for 91 minutes, using a bi-metal bimetal blade with variable pitch at a saw speed of 60 m/min and a cutting width of 3 mm, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Broaching Machine, a lathed part is broached using a pull-type broach with carbide tips to achieve an IT7 tolerance class, producing a broached component, with the operation lasting for 90 minutes, during which the input lathed part is loaded from a MobileRobot and the resulting broached component is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

A broached component is loaded from a conveyor belt onto a horizontal lathe where roughing turning is performed for 97 minutes at a rotation speed of 450 rpm and a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev using a carbide insert (CNMG 432), resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

A lathed part is loaded from a MobileRobot onto a Grinding Machines to perform surface grinding using an aluminum oxide, 60 grit grinding wheel rotating at 1800 m/min with a feed rate of 0.05 mm/pass, transforming the part into a ground part that is then transferred to a ConveyorBelt, taking 24 minutes.

On a Vertical Lathe, the Ground part is subjected to Precision Turning and Drilling for 8 minutes using a CNC programmed contour and center drilling toolpath to achieve IT6 tolerance with a 1.6 μm surface finish, resulting in the Final drilled and shaped part being transferred to a MobileRobot.

The Final drilled and shaped part is shaped using a Shaper machine with a high-speed steel (HSS) shaping tool, a stroke length of 300 mm, and a shaping speed of 25 strokes per minute for 72 minutes, resulting in a Shaped part that is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

On the Gear Shaper, a gear shaping operation forms a spur gear with 24 teeth at a shaping speed of 60 reciprocations per minute, processing the shaped part from the conveyor belt for 54 minutes to produce a shaped gear that is transferred to the mobile robot.

The Laser Cutter performs laser cutting on the Shaped gear, held in the MobileRobot, for 67 minutes, achieving a high precision cut with ±0.05 mm tolerance and producing a smooth, burr-free edge finish with minimal dross, resulting in a CutSheetMetal component placed on the ConveyorBelt.

The honing operation is performed on a Honing Machine, using a 220 grit stone to achieve a bore size of 45.0 mm ± 0.005 mm, processing the cut sheet metal component that arrived via laser on a ConveyorBelt for 63 minutes, resulting in a precision finished part classified as a HonedCylinder now loaded onto a MobileRobot.

Using a Shear (Sheet Metal) machine, a precision finished honed cylinder is sheared into sheet metal through a shearing operation lasting 39 minutes, with a shear angle of 2 degrees, a cutting speed of 10 strokes per minute, and a hardened steel, straight edge blade, transforming the input component carried by a MobileRobot into sheared sheet metal output on a ConveyorBelt.

Using a Punch Press, a sheared sheet metal component is punched with a 12 mm diameter punch at a stroke speed of 80 strokes per minute and automatic die alignment via optical sensor, resulting in a finished sheet metal product, and this operation takes 76 minutes.

The finished sheet metal product is planed on a Planer for 12 minutes, achieving a surface finish of 3.2 μm Ra with a planing depth of 1.5 mm per pass and a feed rate of 0.4 mm/stroke, resulting in a planed part that is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

On a Horizontal Milling Machine, finish milling is performed on a planed part for 1 minute using a milling speed of 1200 rpm and a climb milling tool path with a 5 mm stepover to achieve a surface finish of 1.6 μm Ra, resulting in a finished machined component that is transferred to a mobile robot.

Using a drill press, precision drilling is performed on the finished machined component loaded on a mobile robot, creating holes with a diameter of 8.5 mm and a tolerance of H7 (±0.015 mm), resulting in a finished part with holes that is then transferred to a conveyor belt, taking 7 minutes.

A Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs wire EDM cutting on a finished part with holes, using fine finishing with low current and an integrated deburr cycle, with deionized water having a conductivity of less than 5 μS/cm as the dielectric fluid, for 46 minutes, resulting in a precision finished part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Screw Machines, perform Screw Threading on a Precision finished part loaded from a MobileRobot for 14 minutes, using M10 screw size and Metric coarse (6g tolerance) thread type at a production rate of 120 parts per hour, resulting in a Screwed component of type LathedPart transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

On a Hobbing Machine, a gear hobbing operation is performed on a screwed component loaded from a conveyor belt, using a hobbing speed of 150 rpm and a feed rate of 2 mm/rev to produce an involute gear profile with a 20-degree pressure angle, lasting for 54 minutes, resulting in a hobbied gear that is transferred to a mobile robot.

Using a vertical milling machine, a hobbied gear is finish milled with a circular pocket milling pattern and radial finish pass to achieve a tolerance of ±0.02 mm, resulting in a finished sheet metal product classified as a milled part, which is then placed on a conveyor belt, and the operation takes 66 minutes.

A CNC turning operation is performed on a CNC Turning Center using spindle speed of 650 rpm and CNC program #SHAFT_FIN_01, with tool offsets verified via touch probe, to machine a finished sheet metal product loaded on a conveyor belt into a finished machined component, which is then transferred to a mobile robot, and the process takes 55 minutes.

The Stewart Platform Mills performs multi-axis milling on a finished machined component loaded from a MobileRobot, using a 5-axis simultaneous tool configuration with a ball nose end mill and an active damping system engaged to maintain precision within ±0.005 mm, resulting in a ground part that is transferred to a ConveyorBelt after processing for 42 minutes.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) machine performs a shearing operation on sheet metal, cutting it to size at a cutting speed of 15 meters per minute with a high-carbon steel, hardened blade and a shear angle of 2 degrees, processing the material for 67 minutes and resulting in sheared sheet metal being transferred to a MobileRobot.

Using a drill press, a metal bar is drilled with a 10 mm drill at a spindle speed of 800 rpm and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, producing a drilled component that is placed on a mobile robot, and the operation takes 13 minutes.

The punch press performs a punching operation on a sheet metal component, using a 25 mm diameter punch at a stroke speed of 60 strokes per minute with automatically calibrated die alignment maintaining ±0.05 mm tolerance, processing the material for 74 minutes to produce a finished sheet metal product that is then transferred to a mobile robot.

On a Vertical Lathe, a metal bar is subjected to vertical turning for 38 minutes, using a carbide insert tool (CNMG 432) at a rotation speed of 450 rpm and a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

On the CNC Turning Center, a CNC turning operation is performed on a lathed part for 10 minutes, using CNC program Program_003A, a spindle speed of 1200 rpm, and tool offsets verified via touch probe, resulting in a finished machined component that is transferred to the conveyor belt.

A planed part is surface ground using a grinding machine with an aluminum oxide, 60 grit grinding wheel rotating at 1800 m/min and a feed rate of 0.05 mm/pass, transforming it into a ground part that is then placed on a mobile robot, and the operation takes 67 minutes.

On a Broaching Machine, a metal bar is broached using a pull-type spline broach with a feed rate of 1.2 mm/stroke and a depth of cut of 3 mm, transforming it into a broached component over a duration of 6 minutes, after which the finished part is transferred to a MobileRobot.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs wire EDM cutting on the ground part using deionized water as the dielectric fluid, operating in fine finish mode with low roughness and enabled deburring settings in a double-pass configuration, transforming the ground part into a precision finished part, which is then transferred to a mobile robot, all for 50 minutes.

On a Horizontal Lathe, a metal bar is subjected to horizontal turning for 72 minutes, using a cermet insert, TNMG 16 tool at a rotation speed of 500 rpm and a feed rate of 0.18 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

The horizontal milling machine performs a horizontal milling operation on the milled part, using climb milling with full slotting tool path at a milling speed of 220 m/min to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, lasting for 93 minutes, after which the finished machined component is transferred to the mobile robot.

On a Hobbing Machine, a gear hobbing operation is performed on a broached component loaded from a conveyor belt, machining an involute gear profile with a 20° pressure angle at a hobbing speed of 120 rpm and a feed rate of 0.8 mm/rev, taking 25 minutes to produce a hobbied gear that is then transferred to a mobile robot.

On the Gear Shaper, a broached component is shaped into a spur gear with 36 teeth through the gear shaping operation at a speed of 150 strokes per minute, lasting for 72 minutes, resulting in a shaped gear transported via mobile robot.

The honing machine performs a honing operation on a honed cylinder, using a 220 mesh honing grit to achieve a bore size of 50.00 ± 0.005 mm, lasting for 66 minutes, after which the precision finished part is transferred to a mobile robot.

Using a Bandsaw, a metal bar is cut via bandsaw cutting for 71 minutes, operating at a saw speed of 60 m/min with a bi-metal blade of 4/6 TPI and a cutting width of 3 mm kerf, transforming the input metal bar on the conveyor belt into a lathed part transferred to a mobile robot.

The laser cutter performs laser cutting on sheet metal loaded from the conveyor belt, using a laser power of 2500 W, a cutting speed of 3.5 m/min, and nitrogen gas assist at 18 bar, taking 18 minutes to produce cut sheet metal that is transferred to a mobile robot.

A vertical milling operation is performed on a lathed part using a vertical milling machine at a milling speed of 250 m/min with a 12 mm carbide end mill tool and a depth of cut of 2.5 mm, lasting for 77 minutes, resulting in a milled part that is then placed on a mobile robot.

The milled part is planed on a Planer for 27 minutes, achieving a planing depth of 1.8 mm, a feed rate of 0.3 mm/stroke, and a surface finish of Ra 3.2 µm, resulting in a planed part that is transferred to a MobileRobot.

The milled part is shaped on a Shaper for 20 minutes using a HSS single-point tool at a shaping speed of 40 strokes per minute and a stroke length of 150 mm, resulting in a shaped part that is transferred to a MobileRobot.

On a Screw Machines, Screw Machining is performed on a lathed part to create a screwed component with an M10 metric coarse thread at a production rate of 120 units per hour, taking 97 minutes, after which the output is placed on a MobileRobot.

On the Stewart Platform Mills, a multi-axis milling operation is performed on the milled part retrieved from the ConveyorBelt, using a 5-axis simultaneous tool configuration with a ball nose end mill and an active damping system engaged to minimize vibrations, achieving a milling precision of ±0.005 mm, and upon completion of the 17 minutes of processing, the resulting ground part is transferred to the MobileRobot.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs precision wire cutting on a ground part loaded from a MobileRobot, using fine finish mode, auto-deburr settings, and deionized water as the dielectric fluid, producing a precision finished part that is transferred to a ConveyorBelt, all for 84 minutes.
